themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Today's answers on durable identity resolution all say there is no ground truth for who a person is, echoing the same complaint in answer engine optimization, cross-channel incrementality, generative content review, and lost B2B buying-group signal.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On identity resolution the models say device platforms earn more by keeping their walls up, matching the same reading of agent traffic (agents profit by looking human), journey orchestration (channel bonuses punish coordination), the semantic context layer (teams defend their own definitions), and ad supply integrity (the market profits from fake volume).

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back, and the same single-exit move appears in downstream consent enforcement and in the shared send log proposed for journey orchestration.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers call ad platforms and trained models black boxes that cannot be inspected or made to unlearn, and the same opacity drives the identity resolution, ad supply integrity, and incrementality answers where platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content review answers say implied claims and shifting legal standards cannot be automated, so they constrain generation to approved claims, while the semantic context layer answers insist conflicting definitions of customer are a political settlement no schema can make.
